submitter_note: Kelli Taylor, resident of Calgary-North West
note: 'Bearspaw' here is the Bearspaw acreage area of Rocky View County, not Stoney Nakoda Bearspaw First Nation; 'Samson' is a commissioner.

submitter_note: Amy Shantz, resident of Calgary-Buffalo
community: Treaty 6, 7 and 8 nations (generally); Driftpile mentioned as example
request: do not split treaty areas across district boundaries; keep each treaty's nations within districts that do not straddle treaties (e.g. no district mixing Treaty 8 and Treaty 7)
quote: So if we could avoid altering the treaty boundaries and keep each treaty within a particular boundary, that would be wonderful, I think.
note: Speaker says she does not speak for any nation and consulted none successfully. Request is by treaty area, not a named reserve/district. Also on EB-562: 'I wouldn't want the Slave Lake one to be including part of that upper area and part of ... Treaty 8 and Treaty 7.' Driftpile mentioned only as example of service-centre ties (High Prairie vs Grande Prairie). Final lines: Tsuut'ina sportsplex ties with Calgary (supporting prior speaker), no explicit request.

submitter_note: Graham Sucha, former MLA Calgary-Shaw, resident of Calgary-Glenmore
request: move Tsuut'ina Nation out of the Banff riding and into a Calgary riding (likely Calgary-Glenmore or a shifted Calgary-West), as was done with Enoch in Edmonton-West-Enoch
quote: you may want to consider the integration of Tsuut’ina Nation into Calgary as well with the sort of consideration of communities of interest
note: Says he does not speak for Tsuut'ina. Answered 'Oh, absolutely' to Chair asking if he favours Tsuut'ina becoming like Enoch. Suggests Calgary-Glenmore will have most integration. Asked about separating Tsuut'ina from Stoney Nakoda, says no major impact as distinct cultures (he misstates Stoney Nakoda as Blackfoot). Praises Edmonton-West-Enoch.

submitter_note: Jackie Clayton, Mayor of Grande Prairie
note: No reserve content; 'Samson' is a commissioner, 'reserve' hit is from 'preserve'.

submitter_note: Ken Vanderwell, VP Lesser Slave Lake UCP constituency association, Slave Lake resident
community: Indigenous (Treaty 8) communities of the Lesser Slave Lake division (11 communities, unnamed)
request: keep the existing Lesser Slave Lake division (adding Swan Hills) as a special division, partly because it recognizes its large Indigenous population and Treaty 8 traditional areas
quote: recognizes our large, growing Indigenous population, the Treaty 8 trading and traditional areas.
note: Main request is adding Swan Hills to keep Lesser Slave Lake; the Indigenous/Treaty 8 point is one of five reasons, no reserve named. The text after '[...]' labelled 'Mr. Vanderwell' is actually MLA Scott Cyr (Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul), who says Lesser Slave Lake should stay because 'a lot of it is First Nations and Métis' - not coded here as it is not Vanderwell's words.

submitter_note: Scott Cyr, MLA Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul
note: Only 'First Nations partners' passing mention; his remark that Lesser Slave Lake should stay because much of it is First Nations and Métis appears in record T35-002 (mislabelled). Says Bonnyville-Cold Lake-St. Paul could give up western population to save Lesser Slave Lake.

submitter_note: Brenda Yasinski, Councillor, County of Northern Lights
note: General: keep current representation, as change 'dilutes the voices of rural and remote communities, including the Indigenous communities'. No district arrangement for any nation.

submitter_note: Terry Ungarian, Reeve, County of Northern Lights

quote: this proposal removes the town of Slave Lake, the municipal district of Lesser Slave River, and the Sawridge First Nation from their closest neighbouring communities
note: Objection to interim-report split; neighbours not named precisely (implied High Prairie / rest of current Lesser Slave Lake riding). Also says 'disrupts Indigenous and non-Indigenous neighbours'. Paddle Prairie Métis settlement mentioned only to describe extent of Peace River-Notley.

submitter_note: Todd Beck, CPA, Medicine Hat
note: No reserve content; 'Samson' is a commissioner.

note: First Nations mentioned only re road access and MLA chartering a plane to a First Nation hamlet; asks to leave northern region unchanged, no reserve arrangement.

submitter_note: Tiffany Belesky, Métis, resident of Joussard
community: Indigenous lands/partnerships around Lesser Slave Lake (unnamed)
request: keep Joussard with High Prairie and Slave Lake and keep the Lesser Slave Lake communities under one MLA, taking the area's Indigenous land and partnerships into account
quote: As a First Nations person – I am Métis – we have lots of Indigenous land here. That is something that I hope is taken into consideration.
note: Main request is for Joussard (a hamlet, not a settlement) to stay with the lake communities; Indigenous content is a supporting reason ('Indigenous partnerships' on EB-586 too; 'Communities around the same lake should share the same MLA'). No reserve or settlement named. Says she is Métis; does not name a settlement membership.

submitter_note: Stacey Messner, Mayor of Grimshaw

note: No reserve content.

submitter_note: Francesca Ward, Mayor of Slave Lake, for town council
community: First Nations and Métis communities around Slave Lake: Sawridge, Driftpile, Swan River, Peerless Trout, Whitefish, Loon River, Bigstone, Sucker Creek, Gift Lake Métis settlement
request: keep the Lesser Slave Lake district so the First Nations and Métis communities anchored on Slave Lake are not fragmented across several ridings (and not join Slave Lake to Westlock)
quote: Fragmenting these communities across multiple ridings risks weakening their access to representation and their ability to engage meaningfully with government
note: Municipal speaker, not a nation; refers to the Indian regional council for better evidence. Says 14 First Nations and settlements within 1-1.5 h of Slave Lake, most in current district not the proposed one. Says Sawridge First Nation borders the town. Lists nations in answer to Mr. Evans (EB-590/591).

submitter_note: Jennifer Churchill, Executive Director, Alberta North Central Alliance (5 First Nations + 5 municipalities), co-presenting with Lesser Slave Lake Indian Regional Council
community: Lesser Slave Lake Indian Regional Council nations (Sawridge, Swan River, Driftpile, Sucker Creek) and Bigstone Cree Nation; Métis settlements in Big Lakes county / MD of Opportunity
request: keep the current Lesser Slave Lake riding whole rather than split in three, and do not split Sawridge from the other Lesser Slave Lake Indian Regional Council nations
quote: Your proposal will split Sawridge from the rest of the nations in Lesser Slave Lake Indian Regional Council.
note: ANCA is a joint municipal-First Nations alliance; coded nation_or_council because it includes five First Nations as members and she presents jointly with the LSLIRC executive director (second reader may prefer non_member for ANCA staff). Answered 'Yes, they are' / 'Yes' to Chair's description that all members are in existing Lesser Slave Lake riding and interim report 'blown up' that cohesion. Asks why s.15(2) special status not continued. Record opens with fragments from other speakers (Matthews, Mr. Evans) out of reading order.

submitter_note: Ken Matthews, former reeve/councillor, Big Lakes County
community: three Métis settlements and at least six First Nations within Big Lakes County (unnamed)
request: keep Lesser Slave Lake boundaries as they are (adding all of Big Lakes County incl. Swan Hills) so the county's Métis settlements and First Nations are not separated
quote: It takes out three Métis settlements, three of eight in the province, and at least six First Nations that are within the boundaries of Big Lakes county. It separates them.
note: Settlements and nations not named. Main request is current boundaries plus southward extension to all of Big Lakes County and Swan Hills; objects to county being split among four MLAs. Page label inferred from text order (jumbled reading order).

submitter_note: Mike Evans, Executive Director, Lesser Slave Lake Indian Regional Council
community: Lesser Slave Lake Indian Regional Council nations (four First Nations: Sawridge, Swan River, Driftpile, Sucker Creek), Métis settlements of the region
request: do not split the Lesser Slave Lake constituency; keep the regional council's nations and region together, adding population from neighbouring areas if needed rather than dividing
quote: There’s a very real concern in the Indigenous community that if the constituency is split as proposed, there won’t be an Indigenous representative in any of them
note: Also EB-596/597: 'how difficult would it be to add some areas from neighbouring to change the population without necessarily affecting' and 'maybe that can be addressed in a different way than dividing.' Notes Treaty 8 signed at what is now Sucker Creek reserve; other former member nations now in Grande Prairie ridings and Kee Tas Kee Now Tribal Council (no request about them). Nation names taken from co-presenter's list (T36-006); he says 'four distinct First Nations'.

note: First Nations / Indigenous communities mentioned only as part of rural MLA workload; no arrangement requested.

quote: that seems to me to be a no-brainer to be an area that would be part of Fish Creek because, frankly, that’s the way the land flows

submitter_note: Laura Svab, Mayor of Blackfalds
note: No reserve content; 'Samson' is a commissioner.

submitter_note: Marc Slingerland, resident of Lethbridge
community: Kainai (Blood) reserve; First Nations on-reserve and urban Indigenous populations around Lethbridge
request: create hybrid Lethbridge ridings, with the Kainai reserve joined to a west-Lethbridge hybrid so on-reserve and urban Indigenous people share a representative
quote: The Kainai reserve, obviously, is part of the urban-rural Indigenous population, would come on the west side.
